locator: I q.3 a.4 co., second proof: Oportet igitur quod ipsum esse comparetur ad essentiam quae est aliud ab ipso, sicut actus ad potentiam
interpretation: Esse is the actuality of every form or nature, so an essence other than its esse is in potency to it. The potency belongs to the essence, a principle of the thing; the reading counts it as the thing's being in potency in some respect, matching the article's own conclusion from 'in Deo nihil sit potentiale'. Only the second of the three proofs is formalized.
